title: Enterprise Request Intake — Sales/CS Mini-PRD & Scoped Signal Pipeline
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Goal: Establish a repeatable, lightweight 'first-mile' capture and mini-PRD pipeline that Sales/CS can use to submit enterprise feature requests for non-bug work. The artifact should allow rapid technical scoping, business prioritization, and a go/no-go recommendation within 3 working days. This ticket scopes the template, routing rules, minimal validation, and a short triage rubric that maps requests to intake buckets (Quick Win, Pilot, Strategic, Not Planned).

Problem: Current Sales/CS intake is inconsistent: asks arrive as long emails or Slack threads with missing success metrics, unclear security needs, and no cost sensitivity signal. That causes long back-and-forth, delayed scoping, misprioritized roadmap items, and broken expectations for customers.

Proposal: Deliver a one-page "mini-PRD" template and short pipeline plus a lightweight intake form (Google Form / Confluence form) and a mapping document that defines routing and who owns the next steps. The mini-PRD captures: 1) Ask summary, 2) Customer & account context, 3) Business objective / success metric, 4) Usage patterns (QPS, users, latency), 5) Data sensitivity / compliance, 6) API surface impact, 7) Cost sensitivity (latency vs cost tradeoff), 8) Required rollout constraints (regions/SLA), 9) Quick sketch of engineering risk and rough effort band, 10) Recommended priority.

Outcomes: reduce average time-to-scope from Sales/CS receipt to PM recommendation to <= 3 business days; cut clarifying asks by 60%; create a reliable handoff artifact for ENG/SE to estimate and for GTM to set customer expectations.
capture_template: 1) One-line request summary (what problem does this solve?)
2) Customer / Account & ARR impact (customer name, seat/license, potential upsell)
3) Business objective & success metric (SLOs for business)
4) How will feature be used? (users, frequency, sample QPS, avg tokens)
4b) Latency vs cost sensitivity label (latency-sensitive | cost-sensitive | neutral)
5) API surface changes (new endpoint? param change? embeddings? rerank?)
6) Security / compliance flags (PII, regulated sector, on-prem requirement)
7) Rollout constraints (regions, dedicated capacity, private deploy)
8) Minimal acceptance criteria (what must work in pilot?)
9) Rough effort band (small: 1-2 wks | medium: 2-6 wks | large: >6 wks)
acceptance_criteria: A shareable mini-PRD template available in Confluence + a short intake form linked from the Sales/CS playbook.
Routing rules that assign incoming asks to an owner within 24 hours and categorize into Quick Win / Pilot / Strategic / Not Planned.
A triage rubric spreadsheet that captures initial cost/latency sensitivity and security flags for ENG scoping.
A dashboard widget (Console) or internal tracker with time-to-scope metrics showing baseline and post-launch improvement targets.
Pilot run with 5 incoming enterprise asks from Sales/CS and documented outcomes (decision and next steps)
definition_of_done: Confluence page 'Mini-PRD: Sales/CS Intake' published and linked from CS playbook.
Intake form (Google Form) created and tested; results auto-populate a triage spreadsheet.
Routing automation (Zapier/Slack or internal webhook) notifies owner channel and PM within 1 hour of submission.
Triage rubric and estimation matrix reviewed with ENG/SE and appended to Confluence.
Training email and 30-min runbook session for Sales/CS AEs and CSMs completed and recorded.
